hypothesis: A declared bounded-history prompt projection permits longer native campaigns while retaining current world facts, and allows three small local models to be compared under one common condition.
notes: Use the same digest-bound native starting save, exact model manifests, code, observation/action interfaces and bounds for every model. No rankings from one short attempt.

The packed prompt preserves all current native fields, the exact latest result and model-authored persistent notes. It omits duplicate recent-memory text and older per-target action details, then keeps the largest newest history suffix fitting the unchanged request allowance. Omissions are explicit and full private traces/checkpoints remain retained.
Never truncate the current fortress snapshot to make a request fit. An irreducible oversize snapshot pauses before dispatch at the checkpointable boundary.
The larger per-segment decision count and token allowance distinguish this development condition from the earlier six-decision baseline. This is still not a year-two endurance condition.
No action or simulation advancement is scripted. Zero metered model API charges do not imply zero local hardware, electricity or existing-host costs.

Run models serially with one loaded model and one isolated native game at a time. Temporary processes require teardown; public model weights are reproducible project cache, not committed game evidence.
